Live Animal Exports

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
60,000 sheep on one container ship headed for the Middle East in the middle of their summer... what could possibly go wrong?

Unique Selling Point:
We have footage from Animals Australia about the terrible conditions of live animal exports by sea showing sheep suffering in the heat, knee-deep in faeces, covered in sores. Filmed during 5 voyages between May 2017 and November 2017, over 4,000 sheep died during these voyages - almost half of them from heat stroke. Australia's Live Animal Export business was flourishing for almost 5 decades until wistleblowers (including the state vet) came out with damning evidence of the treatment and conditions of the animals on board the ships. The industry has been placed in the spotlight and tighter controls were put in place after their expose in 2017/18... Fast Forward to 2019... ALMAWASHI, the company in Dubai that is organising the export/import of the sheep to Dubai, Kuwait and Oman have set their sights on SA with a shipment of 60,000 sheep heading for the Middle East in mid-September.

Summary:
ALMAWASHI with the aid of a South African company, Page Farming Trust (Bruce Page) is shipping 60,000 live sheep to Kuwait, Dubai and Oman in mid-September. At the moment close to 50,000 sheep are already in a feedlot in Berlin, outside East London. The sheep are destined to the Middle East for slaughter for the Muslim festivals - especially live slaughter of animals - via the Al Shuwaikh, a vehicle cargo ship that has been "modified" to carry live animals. The ship has 5 levels, all of which will be filled with sheep. The footage shows sheep covered in faeces, sores and dying of heat stroke. We also have footage showing the inhumane treatment of the animals on the other side. Kuwait, Dubai and Oman DO NOT have animal welfare laws and the footage shows horrendous slaughtering, cramming into car boots, and live sales on the side of the road. The Al Shuwaikh is registered in Panama, with a crew from the Philipines. Once the ship is in International waters South Africa's animal welfare legislation can do nothing to help the animals.

Further information:
The Project has been "sold" to government under the pretence of economic upliftment. Most of the sheep come from emerging farmers. The plan is to export a further 600,000 sheep to these countries over the next 3 years. Dr Lynn Simpson served as the on-board vet for some 57 live export voyages, tending as best she could to the needs of animals and humans alike. She was a respected live export vet and was appointed by the Department of Agriculture in Australia in 2012 to oversee live exports. It all became too much for her and she compiled a detailed report on the horrors of the industry, which was leaked. Subsequently she was dismissed from her job. She now works with Animals Australia, a NGO that fights for animal rights. Some of her accounts, and subsequent whistleblowers reveal pregnant sheep aborting because of the stress onboard, animals basically live in their own urine and faeces for the 3-week journey. There is limited ventilation on the ship so many animals die from heat stroke. Dr Simpson reports that in some cases animals that have just died had such high temperatures that their blood would burn her skin. And as if the journey is not enough, the animals often face horrible deaths on the other side. Animals are dragged down the street and slaughtered inhumanely. In 2018 Australia's biggest sheep exporter lost it's license and this is why South Africa has been selected to supply the Middle East with sheep.

Expert:
Ms. Shatha Hamade Animals Australia
Mr. Nazareth Appalsamy NSPCA
Ms. Marcelle Meredith CEO: NSPCA
Dr. Lynn Simpson Veterinarian

Locations:
Johannesburg
East London

Other Footage Sources:
Undercover footage from Animals Australia

Script: LIVE ANIMAL EXPORTS

v/o ETA 20 Sept 2019 The Al Shuwaikh is a massive, 32 year-old Kuwaiti cargo ship currently on its way to South Africa. Its roughly 65-thousand passengers have been assembled on a farm outside East London, unaware of the fate that awaits them. These sheep are about to embark on a 3-week nightmare journey to the Middle East... Shatha Hamade Every animal welfare organisation on the planet opposes the live export trade by sea, and for good reason. The inherent suffering and risk in this trade are actually unavoidable.

v/o The live animal export trade by sea has been big business in Australia for over 5 decades. It’s estimated that more than 200 million Australian sheep have been exported to the Middle East. BUT since its inception in the 1990’s Animals Australia has been opposing the industry for the unnecessary suffering animals endure on long sea voyages. Shatha Hamade is an undercover investigator and legal counsel for Animals Australia. Shatha Hamade This industry has survived this long from Australia because of the veil of secrecy. Nobody has been able to uncover what actually happens on these vessels.

v/o BUT it was veterinarian Dr Lynn Simpson, who had sailed 57 voyages from Australia on board export ships, who first started to lift this “veil of secrecy”...her revelations were shocking. Dr Lynn Simpson On every live export ship the animals do suffer - to one extent or another. Be it generalised accumulated stress from transport, being in a strange environment, the noise of the ships, acclimatising to pellets and food conversion. They suffer diseases, injuries.

v/o Simpson’s concerns were corroborated when a whistleblower recorded undercover footage of the harrowing conditions aboard export vessels including the Al Shuwaikh in the summer of 2017. Dr Lynn Simpson I did 57 voyages. I didn’t just have one bad experience. So, when I started to see that footage and any other footage I’m just seeing the same thing again and again. I’m seeing my experience repeated and repeated.

v/o The undercover footage showed thousands of sheep squeezed into pens, with little or no room to move or even lie down. Sheep standing knee-deep in their own faeces and urine... Dr Lynn Simpson People have to understand that these ships… they’re such an unnatural environment. They’re like a multi-story car park. And when you put animals into this environment, especially in the enclosed decks, which she has many of below the main deck, they generate a lot of heat and a lot of gas. They generate methane and ammonia and CO2 as well as their own body-heat. It’s like being in a crowded elevator.

v/o Most of the footage -- filmed during 5 different voyages -- is so disturbing that we decided not to air it on Carte Blanche. It shows sheep weak from heat exhaustion, collapsing and literally drowning in their own waste. Others have severe injuries, even broken limbs from the overcrowding. It shows ewes aborting because of stress. Many sheep are simply left to die. The intense heat is certainly not the only stress factor, but on one of the voyages it had a severe impact. Shatha Hamade More than 2,400 sheep died from heat stress. What that means is they literally cooked alive and died because of the heat-humidity combination.

v/o It was this footage that finally gave Animals Australia the evidence they needed to deal the industry a severe blow. Shatha Hamade Australia has banned shipments to the Middle East between June, July, August and September because of the heat, humidity extremities on the vessels which cause heat stress suffering. LINK Animals Australia succeeded in restricting the export of sheep on long voyages and tighter controls were put in place. So, exporters looked for a new destination to fill the gap. And South Africa seemed a likely target.

v/o Al Mawashi is the largest buyer of live Australian sheep. Besides banned summer shipments, the company also faces losing cargo from the Al Shuwaikh, which will no longer be allowed to export animals from Down Under to the Middle East as of January 2020. So the company came knocking on South Africa's door and reportedly secured a deal to ship millions of our sheep, live, to the Middle East over the next few years. Nazareth Appalsamy We have heard - through a reliable source - that the Kuwaitis have met with our government last year, with negotiations to trade, however our government denies such talk.

v/o Senior Inspector Nazareth Appalsamy with the NSPCA’s Farm Animal Protection Unit, says they met with a representative from Al Mawashi earlier this year. Nazareth Appalsamy Derek: What are their plans when it comes to exports from South Africa? Well they made it very clear. Their intention for the year 2019 was two consignments of sheep averaging between 65,000 and a maximum of 75, 000. So, we’re looking at around 130,000 sheep for 2019. Then shockingly he told us that they intend importing over the next three to 5 years 600,000 animals annually made up of sheep, goats and cattle.

v/o South Africa regularly export animals to Mauritius. In the late 1990s and again in 2012 Carte Blanche exposed the appalling treatment of cattle during their voyage to the island. Nazareth Appalsamy We know for a fact that the ammonia levels get so high on these ships that these animals have respiratory problems. We know that stocking densities are often compromised so that one gets more money for larger consignments. Nazareth Appalsamy We know that conditions at sea are sometimes rough and that animals experience motion sickness.

v/o The South African exporter responsible for most of our livestock exports to Mauritius, and this new deal with the Kuwaiti company, is Bruce Page of the Page Farming Trust. Nazareth Appalsamy Page Farming Trust is the facilitator or if you want to call him the partner. Basically his job is to source these animals throughout the country and to be responsible for getting them onboard the vessel. Page refused an on-camera interview. However, he did confirm that the sheep were sourced from emerging farmers and he said they were ready to go... he maintained that he had no knowledge of what would happen to the sheep once they were handed over to the crew of the Al Shuwaikh. Bruce Page Look I don’t know. I can’t tell you. I’ve never been on the vessel, I don’t know. Look, the job that I am doing, I’m doing the best I can. So, we’re just doing the best we can on this side. Legally, Page has ticked all the necessary boxes for this impending export. Ethically, the question is whether not knowing what is going to happen to the sheep, is an adequate defence? Shatha Hamade I challenge the farmer that might be contracting with the Kuwaiti company. I challenge him to sit down and watch this footage and talk to me and tell me that he thinks that it’s okay. When we offered to send Page the footage, he declined to engage in any way. But for the sheep, the nightmare will not end once they dock in Kuwait. Shatha Hamade

Derek: What conditions have you seen on the other side when it comes to the way that they are slaughtered? Since 2013 I have been conducting undercover investigations in importing countries, mainly Kuwait and countries around the Middle East. Well, first of all these animals are exported to countries that don’t have animal protection laws…. Shatha Hamade The sheep are literally trussed and dragged and stuffed into car boots in incredible heat to be taken home for home slaughter. Alternatively they’re slaughtered on filthy concrete blocks in chaotic livestock markets or they’re taken and slaughtered in slaughterhouses.

Derek: Aren’t these just the exceptional cases? No. So all sheep that enter into Kuwait and the Middle East are killed fully conscious, and usually from what I see, and from what we gather in terms of our investigations, the slaughtermen are not skilled and it usually takes multiple stabs and cuts before the animal dies. Nazareth Appalsamy

Derek: Nazareth, how do you feel about what you’ve seen regarding the shipment of these animals? I feel it’s not necessary for animals to be transported via sea for them only to be slaughtered in another country without them being pre-stunned. v/o FOR NSPCA CEO Marcelle Meredith the welfare of the sheep is THE main priority. They want a win-win outcome for all parties involved. Marcelle Meredith I tell you how it would be financially viable for South Africa, is if we slaughter the animals in South Africa and we send the meat over to Kuwait, Oman and Dubai. Let’s export more meat. Then it’s a win for South Africa. Economically and to hold their head up high when it comes to animal welfare...

v/o We tracked the progress of the Al Shuwaikh via satellite and by Thursday it was still on course, making its way down the East coast of Africa. At the moment the only thing standing between the sheep and their final voyage is an official stamp from the South African government. Nazareth Appalsamy The Department of Agriculture needs to issue a health certificate. To our knowledge they have not yet.

v/o The SA Department of Agriculture responded to us in writing -- it is aware of the intended exportation. “The Department is working closely with the NSPCA and we are currently evaluating the documents supplied by the exporters and all other evidence for and against the exportation and we are not yet at a point where we can support the exportation.” After the High Court recently ruled in its favour over the controversial lion bone export quota, the NSPCA is determined to ensure that the Al Shuwaikh will not leave with any of our sheep. Nazareth Appalsamy The court ruled that the government did not take welfare into consideration and we would take the exact same stance if the government gave the green light for this Kuwait ship to dock and load in our country. We will approach the highest court in this land in an attempt to stop this consignment. Marcelle Meredith We will do anything that it takes. If we have to go the legal route, then we will go the legal route. And I’m afraid that that will be against the government.

To our knowledge they have not yet. v/o The SA Department of Agriculture responded to us in writing -- it is aware of the intended exportation. “The Department is working closely with the NSPCA and we are currently evaluating the documents supplied by the exporters and all other evidence for and against the exportation and we are not yet at a point where we can support the exportation.” After the High Court recently ruled in its favour over the controversial lion bone export quota, the NSPCA is determined to ensure that the Al Shuwaikh will not leave with any of our sheep. Nazareth Appalsamy The court ruled that the government did not take welfare into consideration and we would take the exact same stance if the government gave the green light for this Kuwait ship to dock and load in our country. We will approach the highest court in this land in an attempt to stop this consignment. Marcelle Meredith We will do anything that it takes. If we have to go the legal route, then we will go the legal route. And I’m afraid that that will be against the government.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): 60,000 sheep on one container ship headed for the Middle East in the middle of their summer... what could possibly go wrong?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have footage from Animals Australia about the terrible conditions of live animal exports by sea showing sheep suffering in the heat, knee-deep in faeces, covered in sores. Filmed during 5 voyages between May 2017 and November 2017, over 4,000 sheep died during these voyages - almost half of them from heat stroke. Australia's Live Animal Export business was flourishing for almost 5 decades until wistleblowers (including the state vet) came out with damning evidence of the treatment and conditions of the animals on board the ships. The industry has been placed in the spotlight and tighter controls were put in place after their expose in 2017/18... Fast Forward to 2019... ALMAWASHI, the company in Dubai that is organising the export/import of the sheep to Dubai, Kuwait and Oman have set their sights on SA with a shipment of 60,000 sheep heading for the Middle East in mid-September.
metadata.Summary: ALMAWASHI with the aid of a South African company, Page Farming Trust (Bruce Page) is shipping 60,000 live sheep to Kuwait, Dubai and Oman in mid-September. At the moment close to 50,000 sheep are already in a feedlot in Berlin, outside East London. The sheep are destined to the Middle East for slaughter for the Muslim festivals - especially live slaughter of animals - via the Al Shuwaikh, a vehicle cargo ship that has been "modified" to carry live animals. The ship has 5 levels, all of which will be filled with sheep. The footage shows sheep covered in faeces, sores and dying of heat stroke. We also have footage showing the inhumane treatment of the animals on the other side. Kuwait, Dubai and Oman DO NOT have animal welfare laws and the footage shows horrendous slaughtering, cramming into car boots, and live sales on the side of the road. The Al Shuwaikh is registered in Panama, with a crew from the Philipines. Once the ship is in International waters South Africa's animal welfare legislation can do nothing to help the animals.
metadata.Further information: The Project has been "sold" to government under the pretence of economic upliftment. Most of the sheep come from emerging farmers. The plan is to export a further 600,000 sheep to these countries over the next 3 years. Dr Lynn Simpson served as the on-board vet for some 57 live export voyages, tending as best she could to the needs of animals and humans alike. She was a respected live export vet and was appointed by the Department of Agriculture in Australia in 2012 to oversee live exports. It all became too much for her and she compiled a detailed report on the horrors of the industry, which was leaked. Subsequently she was dismissed from her job. She now works with Animals Australia, a NGO that fights for animal rights. Some of her accounts, and subsequent whistleblowers reveal pregnant sheep aborting because of the stress onboard, animals basically live in their own urine and faeces for the 3-week journey. There is limited ventilation on the ship so many animals die from heat stroke. Dr Simpson reports that in some cases animals that have just died had such high temperatures that their blood would burn her skin. And as if the journey is not enough, the animals often face horrible deaths on the other side. Animals are dragged down the street and slaughtered inhumanely. In 2018 Australia's biggest sheep exporter lost it's license and this is why South Africa has been selected to supply the Middle East with sheep.
